body:
I'd like to use this bug as a forum to discuss an extended API to solve this and [other newly uncovered limitations of `st.cache`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/153).

A couple thoughts:

## Is this a problem with `ignore_hash`?

**No.** The goal of `ignore_hash` is to expand the _range_ of objects that can be stored in the cache by allowing objects which are unhashable (like Tensorflow Sessions and Websocket connections).

**But it is a problem with the _name_ `ignore_hash`** which, confusingly, seems like what we should turn on to solve the problem described above. (You can see a more "pure python" example of this problem in [#153](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/153).)

### Possible Solution: `allow_output_mutation` 

Deprecate the name `ignore_hash` and switch to `allow_output_mutation` which I think captures the correct semantics.

## So then would the solution be `allow_input_mutation`? 

**I don't think so.** The point of the cache is that it's like a symbol table parameterized by the input arguments. For example, if you have

```python
@st.cache
def f(x, y):
  ...
```

and you call

```python
z1 = f(X1, Y1)
z2 = f(X2, Y2)
```

then the cache is like a symbol table containing

```
hash(f, X1, Y1, ...) -> z1
hash(f, X2, Y2, ...) -> z2
```

If you allow input mutations, then it's the [same basic problem as having mutable keys in a dictionary](http://effbot.org/pyfaq/why-must-dictionary-keys-be-immutable.htm): you loose the ability to recall earlier symbols. For example if `hash(f, X1, Y1, ...) != hash(f, X1, Y1, ...)` after calling `f(X1, Y1)`, then the value of `z1` has irretrievably be "lost" in the cache! 

**Neither shoud we completely [skip "check\[ing\] inputs when pulling from the cache"](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/157#issue-496566927)**. You need to hash _something_ to parameterize the caches "symbol table."

For example, at minimum you might want to hash the funnction name, but that is not how hashing works right now, so we're introducing completely new semantics, and probably not hashing what the user expects.

### Possible Solution: `hash_by_id`

Really the issue here is that the object isn't hash code can't be trusted. 

Normally, this would involve [overriding `__hash__` and `__eq__` methods](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#object.__hash__) but [Streamlit doesn't use Python's built-in hashing API](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/1d7f6cff6acc7643a6b1f24f2c502f365c4af193/lib/streamlit/hashing.py#L238). Instead, this would involve overring the [Buffer API](https://jakevdp.github.io/blog/2014/05/05/introduction-to-the-python-buffer-protocol/) which I don't understand. Maybe @domoritz can chime in here?

The fully general solution here would be to allow the user to define a custom buffer function _post facto_, but that's too general for now.

Instead I think **we should define a set of types which are hashed by their memory location** either because

- they are immutable anyway, so this is a optimization
- we trust the user to know what they're doing

 Call this list `hash_by_id`. We could specify which types should be thusly hashed as an argument to `st.cache`. So the code above would look like:

```python
@st.cache(cache_by_id=[spacy.lang.en.English])
def process_text(nlp, text):
    ...
```

or we could even offer a method to cache by argument name:

```python
@st.cache(cache_args_by_id=['nlp'])
def process_text(nlp, text):
    ...
```

### A big side benefit: less `ignore_hash=True`

A potential side benefit of this approach would be hard code Tensorflow Sessions and some other type in the global `hash_by_id` set, which would then mean that we could avoid the need for `ignore_hash=True` in many cases.

## Summary

I think the way forward is to:

1. [Treat implicit and explicit inputs equally](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/153).
2. Deprecated `ignore_hash` and replace it with `allow_output_mutation`.
3. Add a `hash_by_id` argument to `st.cache` which would apply to all hashing operations, explicit input, implicit input, and output.

I would welcome @tvst and @domoritz's thoughts on this proposal.

issue.body:
# Summary

I have detected a [snippet of code](https://gist.github.com/treuille/c84d78967b9ddc9474ed53054fa0efee) which behaves differently when run
locally vs from a URL. The issue has to do with whether Streamlit hashes implicit imports to a cached funnction.

## Steps to reproduce

### Test Case 1: Run the code locally

1. Copy this [snippet of code](https://gist.github.com/treuille/c84d78967b9ddc9474ed53054fa0efee) into a file called `cache_bug.py` and run:
```
streamlit run cache_bug.py
```
2. Play with the sliders.
3. **Notice that the output changes _both_ when `x` _and_ `y` change, the correct behavior.**

### Test Case 2: Run the code remotely

1. Run:
```
streamlit run https://gist.githubusercontent.com/treuille/c84d78967b9ddc9474ed53054fa0efee/raw/ca6547a66d481efe5b34a87783a8de7ecc2a4c91/cache_bug.py
```
2. Play with the sliders.
3. **Notice that changing `y` does not change the output!**

# Behavior


## Expected behavior
Both cases should behave identically. The behavior in _Test Case 1_ is correct.

## Actual behavior
_Test Case 2_ behaves incorrectly, as described above.

## Is this a regression?
No.

# Debug info
I'm using a version beyond 0.35 on the `develop` branch:
```
$ streamlit version && python --version && pyenv --version && sw_vers && "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --version

```
Latest commit:
```

commit 670de52f1f10afca228da22c97e56b1356e5172b
Author: Felix Geilert <root92@live.de>
Date:   Thu Sep 19 21:53:03 2019 +0200
```

issue.title: `ignore_cache=True` warning should read `ignore_hash=True`

repository.name: streamlit
repository.description: Streamlit — A faster way to build and share data apps.

issue.body:
# Summary

When users [have a problem with caching, they [often see a warning](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/on-refresh-database-app-errors-out/344/6?u=adrien_treuille) which says `ignore_cache=True` it should read `ignore_hash=True`, which is the [correct keyword argument](https://streamlit.io/docs/api.html?highlight=cache#streamlit.cache).

# Future Work

Eventually, we should rename this deprecated `ignore_hash` and [rename it](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/412)  `allow_output_mutation`.

issue.title: Rename ignore_hash to allow_output_mutation

issue.body:
The `ignore_hash` argument in `@st.cache(ignore_hash=True)` is misnamed, since it does not ignore hashes in all places where `st.cache` uses them. See [this](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/157#issuecomment-533831071) for more information.

We should rename `ignore_hash` to `allow_output_mutation` to make it clearer.

Also: to ease people's migration to the new name we should throw a nice error when users use the old `ignore_hash` kwarg. Something like:
```
The `ignore_hash` argument has been renamed to `allow_output_mutation`.

[traceback]
```

body: This bug is now pretty out of date vis-a-vis the current state of Streamlit, since we've heavily restructured how cacheing works. The repro code used now results in an UnhashableTypeError -- which is expected.
